name: LA-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district (R+17 PVI) with incumbent Mike Johnson running
Johnson's massive financial edge: $21M raised and $9.6M on hand versus ~$269K for the top Democrat
Prediction markets price Johnson at 94% to win
No public polling; race draws little outside attention
model.rationale: This northwest Louisiana seat leans heavily Republican, and Speaker Mike Johnson returns as an incumbent with a dominant fundraising advantage and no serious outside spending against him. Markets and the district's fundamentals both point to an easy Republican hold, with Democratic challengers Gromlich and Cable poorly funded.
model.watch: Any major national backlash event or unexpected scandal involving Johnson could narrow the margin, though an upset remains very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Louisiana's 4th District is a solidly Republican seat, and Speaker Mike Johnson is running for reelection with every structural advantage. The district's partisan lean sits around seventeen points to the right, and Johnson brings the weight of a national profile plus roughly $9.6 million in cash on hand. His Democratic challengers, Matt Gromlich and Conrad Cable, have each raised under $270,000 with minimal reserves, and no outside groups are spending against the incumbent.

Prediction markets give Johnson about a 94 percent chance of winning, and no public polls or expert ratings flag the race as competitive. The forecast expects Johnson to win comfortably, with the main question being the size of his margin rather than the outcome.
